docs.title: serializable
docs.text: Save Python objects as JSON and reconstruct the same classes, including nested objects. Use DataclassSerializable for dataclasses and Serializable for classes whose constructor arguments describe their state.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install serializable

Python 3.9 or later is required.

docs.title: Save and reload an object
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from serializable import DataclassSerializable

@dataclass
class Point(DataclassSerializable):
    x: float
    y: float

point = Point(1.0, 2.0)
restored = Point.from_json(point.to_json())
print(point.to_dict())
print(restored)
print(restored == point)

{'x': 1.0, 'y': 2.0}
Point(x=1.0, y=2.0)
True

to_dict() describes constructor fields. to_json() also records the class and its module so from_json() can reconstruct it. The dataclass keeps its normal generated constructor, equality and representation.

docs.title: Choose a representation
docs.text:
Your task Interface Serialize a dataclass DataclassSerializable Serialize a constructor-based class Serializable Serialize a nested collection of supported objects to_json() / from_json() helpers Obtain constructor fields to_dict() / from_dict()

See save existing classes and files, then change field names. The API reference lists the complete interfaces.

docs.title: Format and limitations
docs.text:
This is a Python object round-trip format, rather than a language-independent application schema. Deserialization imports the recorded module and looks up the class, so that module and class must remain available in the loading environment. Load representations from sources you trust: reconstruction imports modules and calls constructors.

Supported values include primitive values, dictionaries, lists, tuples, sets and objects implementing the serialization interface. Dictionary keys beginning with two underscores are reserved by the format. to_dict() is the object's field mapping; it does not by itself guarantee an ordinary JSON-compatible mapping when those fields contain nested Python objects.

docs.title: Choose a base class
docs.text: Use the dataclass mixin to preserve dataclass-generated methods. The original base class supplies its own constructor-field introspection and object methods.

docs.title: DataclassSerializable
docs.text:
Mixin providing to_dict / from_dict / to_json / from_json for @dataclass-decorated subclasses, without overriding the dunder methods that @dataclass generates.

Subclasses may set _SERIALIZABLE_KEYWORD_ALIASES to migrate old field names across releases: map an old name to the new name, or to None to drop it on load. This mirrors the same hook on Serializable.

docs.title: to_dict
docs.text:
to_dict()

Return a dict mapping each dataclass field name to its current value. Keys match the __init__ keyword arguments, so cls(**obj.to_dict()) reconstructs an equal instance.

docs.title: from_dict classmethod
docs.text:
from_dict(state_dict)

Reconstruct an instance from a to_dict-shaped dictionary, applying _SERIALIZABLE_KEYWORD_ALIASES for backwards compat.

docs.title: __reduce__
docs.text:
__reduce__()

Pickle via the same to_dict / from_dict path used for JSON so pickled objects round-trip even when field order or internal representation changes between releases. Pickles written before serializable 1.2.0 call from_serializable_repr instead, which remains supported.

docs.title: Serializable
docs.text:
Base class for user-defined objects which provides default methods such as to_json, from_json, reduce, and from_dict

Relies on the keys of to_dict() matching the arguments to init.

docs.title: to_dict
docs.text:
to_dict()

Returns a dictionary which can be used to reconstruct an instance of a derived class (typically by matching args to init). The values of the returned dictionary must be primitive atomic types (bool, string, int, float), primitive collections (int, list, tuple, set) or instances of Serializable.

The default implementation is to assume all the positional arguments to init have fields of the same name on a serializable object. Keyword-only arguments are excluded, so they can be used for constructor options which aren't part of the serialized state.

docs.title: from_dict classmethod
docs.text:
from_dict(state_dict)

Given a dictionary of flattened fields (result of calling to_dict()), returns an instance. Does not modify state_dict.

docs.title: to_json
docs.text:
to_json()

Returns a string containing a JSON representation of this object.

docs.title: from_json classmethod
docs.text:
from_json(json_string)

Reconstruct an instance from a JSON string.

docs.title: write_json_file
docs.text:
write_json_file(path)

Serialize this object to JSON and write it to the text file at path.

docs.title: read_json_file classmethod
docs.text:
read_json_file(path)

Construct an instance of this class from the JSON file at path.

docs.title: __reduce__
docs.text:
__reduce__()

Overriding this method directs the default pickler to reconstruct this object using our from_dict method, so pickles survive the same changes to a class (e.g. renamed keywords) as JSON does. Values in to_dict() are pickled natively.

Pickles written before serializable 1.2.0 call from_serializable_repr instead, which remains supported.

docs.title: Serialize supported values
docs.text: The helpers also work with containers. The serializable representation records Python types; the plain field dictionary and JSON string have different roles.

docs.title: to_dict
docs.text:
to_dict(obj)

If value isn't a primitive scalar or collection then it needs to either implement to_dict (instances of Serializable) or have member data matching each required arg of init.

docs.title: to_json
docs.text:
to_json(x)

Returns JSON representation of a given Serializable instance or other primitive object.

docs.title: from_json
docs.text:
from_json(json_string)

Inverse of to_json. Objects are reconstructed bottom-up while parsing, equivalent to (but faster than) from_serializable_repr(json.loads(...)).

docs.title: to_serializable_repr
docs.text:
to_serializable_repr(x)

Convert an instance of Serializable or a primitive collection containing such instances into serializable types.

docs.title: from_serializable_repr
docs.text:
from_serializable_repr(x)

Inverse of to_serializable_repr. Does not modify x.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
Follow the PyEnsembl writing guide and the mhctools example.

Put installation and the first useful example on the home page. Give complete imports and concrete inputs, explain the result, and state prerequisites before the reader runs a command. Show output only when it has been checked. Label replaceable paths and templates.

Order guides by common tasks before advanced setup and implementation details. Keep desktop sidebar groups expanded initially and individually collapsible. Split a page when a substantial task or reference needs its own explanation. Preserve useful old links and anchors when moving content.

Use ordinary text for concepts and library names; reserve inline code for literal commands, API names, parameters, paths and values. Keep qualifications, experimental status and scientific limitations beside the claims they qualify.

Use system fonts, a readable line length and restrained headings. Let wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their containers. Avoid repetitive navigation lists in prose and excessive callouts.

Install requirements-docs.txt and run ./docs.sh before opening a PR. Review the home page and a reference page at desktop and narrow widths. Run the repository's required lint and test commands and execute complete examples. Documentation dependencies are separate from runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Change field names
docs.text:
Use _SERIALIZABLE_KEYWORD_ALIASES when constructor fields change. Both base classes support this mapping: an old name maps to its replacement, or to None when the field should be discarded. A value already provided under the new name takes precedence.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar
from serializable import DataclassSerializable

@dataclass
class Sample(DataclassSerializable):
    name: str
    _SERIALIZABLE_KEYWORD_ALIASES: ClassVar[dict] = {
        "label": "name",
        "obsolete": None,
    }

print(Sample.from_dict({"label": "tumor", "obsolete": 7}))
print(Sample.from_dict({"label": "old", "name": "new"}))

Sample(name='tumor')
Sample(name='new')

The mapping changes constructor keywords; it does not migrate module names or class names recorded in JSON. Keep the recorded class importable, or provide an explicit application-level migration for stored representations.

docs.title: Constructor-based classes
docs.text:
Inherit from Serializable when you already have a normal constructor. Store an attribute for each positional constructor argument, or implement to_dict() with keys that the constructor accepts. Keyword-only arguments (after *) are left out of the default to_dict(), so they can hold constructor options which aren't part of the saved state.

from serializable import Serializable

class Sample(Serializable):
    def __init__(self, name, count):
        self.name = name
        self.count = count

sample = Sample("tumor", 3)
restored = Sample.from_json(sample.to_json())
print(restored.name, restored.count)

tumor 3

The base class supplies equality and a representation from the stored fields. For dataclasses, use the dataclass mixin to retain the methods generated by the dataclass decorator.

docs.title: Save JSON to a file
docs.text:
Continuing the preceding example, use the constructor-based class's file helpers. This example uses a temporary directory so it does not overwrite an existing file.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "sample.json"
    sample.write_json_file(path)
    restored = Sample.read_json_file(path)
    print(restored == sample)

True

DataclassSerializable provides JSON string methods, without the file helpers. For a dataclass, write object.to_json() with Path.write_text() and reload the text with YourClass.from_json().

docs.title: Pickle objects
docs.text:
Pickling uses the same to_dict() and from_dict() methods as JSON, so renamed fields are handled the same way. Pickles written by versions before 1.2.0 can still be loaded.

import pickle

restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(sample))
print(restored == sample)

True

docs.title: Nested objects and collections
docs.text:
Module-level helpers serialize supported containers as well as individual objects. Continuing with sample from above:

from serializable import from_json, to_json

restored = from_json(to_json({"samples": [sample]}))
print(restored["samples"][0].name)

tumor

Keep each object's class importable when loading it in another process. A notebook or a script's local class is a convenient demonstration; a class in an importable module is preferable for persisted data shared across programs.
